explanations.3: This tells apt (the package installer) to run in non-interactive mode so it won't pause waiting for user input during the build.
explanations.9: After installing packages, we delete the cached package lists to shrink the final image size since we won't need them again.
explanations.14: The -fsSL flags tell curl to fail silently on errors, show no progress bar, and follow redirects—useful for reliable automated downloads.
explanations.16: We pipe the downloaded tar file directly to tar extraction instead of saving it to disk first, which is faster and cleaner.
explanations.28: The dd command creates a dummy 200KB file to simulate a real binary; status=none suppresses the progress output so the build log stays clean.
explanations.35: The -i flag runs bash in interactive mode so you get a shell prompt when you enter the container, not just execute and exit.
